steps.content: Word of the Purge Order is out, casting a shadow of despair over the refugee camps.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Let the reports from all the outposts come to me. Stay calm. We have prepared for this. Let's approach this one step at a time.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Everything's on track—supplies, pathways, and network connections. But Greta, what's the status on the meds?

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: We're swamped with injuries, and our friends from the Outlands just brought in their last batch of supplies. Looks like they won't be able to make it through again.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: I made another journey to SALVA. Nurse Anne really helped us out with a bunch of meds, and Dr. Iron was busy with a ton of emergency prosthetic surgeries. They're pushing their limits, I hope they can keep up.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: And... Lavina, are you sure you're okay?

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: The Black Ring's changed completely. Even with the leader back, we couldn't get shackles back to how they were.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: You collapsed due to the pollution a little while ago, and now, with more and more refugees coming in and everyone's on edge. You've got a mountain of tasks weighing on you, you—

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: I'm fine. I handled Drifter Camp, didn't I? I can do the same here.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: We have only 46 hours left. With so many people in Syndicate, we need to act quickly to mobilize more people.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: The kids in the camp are pitching in too, copying flyers with Raye's poems. She always knew how to lift spirits, right?

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: The Homeless are trying their best. We'll save as many as we can.
She gives a small, comforting smile to anxious Greta, then heads off to the wounded area.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...Donald... Hecate...
He barely manages to open his eyes, scanning his surroundings, and there it is—a face that is warm and familiar, yet inexplicably daunting.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...Lavina?

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: No... Sorry... I got the wrong person...

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: I know who you are.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: ...That's all in the past. If you're feeling up to it, we could really use your help; we're stretched thin.
In the quiet that follows, Samuel hands over a map, with a few points in the WhiteSands sketched out, simple but unmistakable.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...Over at Eastside, Quinn has established a few makeshift settlements in WhiteSands, giving us all a place to take shelter.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: That's a huge relief, thanks. I'll handle the coordination.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: One more thing.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Hecate made it back safely, all thanks to you. You don't owe me any more apologies.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: <size=30> I... I don't have the right.</size>
She speaks the last few words in a hushed tone, then turns to leave.

The common folks can't endure the surface much longer—the contamination's too intense. Anyone who doesn't find shelter fast enough soon turns into Corruptors. The Homeless have had to quit their street rounds, now only handing out flyers in the limited safe spots left.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: ...Don't worry, every little bit helps. Let's snap some photos and get them up on the web.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: People in Eastside are watching. Someone is—
Suddenly, a man snatches the flyer right out of Ica's hand.

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: Forget about it. The Executive Officer's severed all our connections. Where are you gonna send it to, huh? And say it does get through, what good are those "good-hearted" Eastsiders? Just a bunch of noise and no action.

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: Do you actually believe you kids can make a difference? Imagine, if I gave you a thrashing right here—how unfair that'd be. Would anyone bother to intervene?

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: Better run while you still can on those two legs. Scram, and fast. You're just a nuisance to look at.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: I won't go! After I see you all off, I'm staying here! I won't just ditch my mom and dad and flee!

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: Your folks are long gone! The writer of those pathetic poems too! Only someone as gullible as you would fall for her stuff!!

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: You're just a kid, what impact do you think you can make? Can hugging those worthless poems really turn things around? Can they ever protect you from the Purge Order?!
Clang!

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Excuse me. I'm your ride outta here, one of the convoy crew. A <color=#fb9259>kid</color>.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: If you're terrified and looking for a way out, get your bags and family sorted. Keep your wits about you, form an orderly line, and register here with me.

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: Haha... So, Zoya's out of the picture, and now you're resorting to a shorty for rescue?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Yeah, yeah, whatever you say. I'm up to my ears here. If you're not gonna help, at least don't stand in the way.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: You've got a voice that carries; rather than barking at those kids, how about you wash out your mouth and give me a hand hollering for attention?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Remember the chat we had earlier?

steps.speaker: Dejected Refugee
steps.content: Ehh...
It is like hitting a nerve for him. He clicks his tongue, clams up, snatches Ica's bag, and just takes off.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...You're the shorty from the Legion, huh?
Horo has gotten a bit taller, really, but she doesn't waste time explaining that. She just looks off towards Ica, standing a little ways off.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: That little guy was so riled up that he was nearly in tears. You're not gonna back him up? Isn't he one of your crew?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Back him up for what? The guy wasn't exactly lying. I'm not naive enough to think a couple of sappy poems mean the world's all sunshine and rainbows.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: And besides, the Homeless aren't under my command; I'm just like them, a bunch of kids without a proper home.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: What about you? Haven't seen your kind around Syndicate for ages. Did the Legion call it quits?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Of course not! The Legion Commander's right here. The 9th Agency shipped us off, so we found something to do out there. Convoy work is old hat for us.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Then, this guy, an executive officer, told me to take down a satellite town early. We've got enough of Hypercubes for now. You can stay with us for a while till you all find your way.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Everyone's counting on me to get you out of here.
Crache sees that Horo is also affected by the shackles, but she looks cool as a cucumber.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Really? You seem like the right person for it. Those kids are your responsibility now. I've got other stuff to handle.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: You're not leaving with us?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...Like I've said before, I'm not one for those naive fairy tales.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Hmm~ You seem to be in the same camp with that downbeat guy. Oh, and just so you know, he came to me just now. Told me he's caught Mania, doesn't think he's got much time left and isn't planning on leaving.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: He insisted on freeing up his spot in the car for someone else, particularly those kids who've got their whole lives ahead. Urged me to get you out fast, so you don't end up dying here.
...Crache stays silent and just walks off.
Miss Matilda, you have to come back, regardless. It's what your aunt has decided.
The Cavendishes aren't meant to meet their end under the Black Ring.
...Matilda glances over to see Corso brooding nearby. Her spirits have been low ever since their clash with Paradeisos.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Corso, we're all set. You can make your move to Eastside.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: What Eastside?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Didn't you always ask me to get you to Eastside? Everything's in place now, time for your getaway.
Corso takes a moment to think, and then, with a sudden understanding, gives a derisive chuckle.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Ha, you think I'm leaving because I'm scared to die? Don't lump me in with those weaklings.
She is visibly irritated, a complete turnaround from how she was before.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: It's these ever-hesitant, spineless wimps I can't stand, and that's why I don't want to be here.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Sure, those Rustfire guys are single-minded, obsessed with those shackles. But at least they are not all talk—they're willing to fight and actually want to fight.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Unlike these cowards today. Just looking at them is irritating.
She looks at the people huddled and shivering in the refugee camp, as if they are too scared to live unless they cling together.
Corso never bothers with the weak before, but now, she's inexplicably on edge, their sobs and whimpers driving her up the wall.
Matilda checks her watch.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Just 46 hours to go...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The blockade has been critically compromised, with BR-002 expanding faster than ever. FAC is desperately trying to rein in the Black Ring to prevent the Purge Order. But they've got a deadline: evacuate the West District within 40 hours.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The 9th Agency, along with Paradeisos's elite, are en route to the Black Ring, likely targeting the Underground. This time, they seem ready to pull out all the stops, possibly even breaking into the Black Ring.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The Executive Committee remaining here is probably going to carry out the Purge Order.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Where is Chief?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: He's taking care of Hecate and Hella. When the Black Ring burst, those two kids were under a lot of stress.
steps.female_content: She's taking care of Hecate and Hella. When the Black Ring burst, those two kids were under a lot of strain.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Even if he regains consciousness, the shackles remain contaminated with BR-002's corruption. And ${PlayerName} isn't having a easy time either.
steps.female_content: Even if she regains consciousness, the shackles remain contaminated with BR-002's corruption. And ${PlayerName} isn't having a easy time either.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Plus...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm not part of Rustfire, not your leader either. I'm not in a position to save anyone.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sorry, please give me some room.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Lavina mentions that ${PlayerName} used to be a warm and gentle person. However, the way he is now gives off a strong sense of aloofness, which is unsettling.
steps.female_content: Lavina mentions that ${PlayerName} used to be a warm and gentle person. However, the way she is now gives off a strong sense of aloofness, which is unsettling.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Over the past few months, Chief's psyche has been relentlessly influenced by the Mania. Now that he's awakened... is he still the same person he used to be?
steps.female_content: Over the past few months, Chief's psyche has been relentlessly influenced by the Mania. Now that she's awakened... is she still the same person she used to be?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: ...He's with Hella and Hecate now, so everything should be fine. I'm sure he's still his old self.
steps.female_content: ...She's with Hella and Hecate now, so everything should be fine. I'm sure she's still her old self.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Since the Black Ring has already erupted, there's no need for him to repay us anymore. Let him take a break.
steps.female_content: Since the Black Ring has already erupted, there's no need for her to repay us anymore. Let her take a break.

steps.speaker: Black Ring Avatar
steps.content: It's all over—the Ring's gained too much power, the White Cube is no match for it now. The entire West District is feeding on its strength. This time, it's unbeatable—not by Paradeisos, not by the Underground, not by that person either, and certainly not by you...

steps.speaker: Black Ring Avatar
steps.content: It's always the same with you, always a step behind, too late to make a difference.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: When all is said and done, it's me who's always one step behind.
The adjutant attempts to say something, but Donald rises by himself, casually stretching his arms.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Time to kick off the escape plan! Good thing we're ready for this.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: I've got a line in with a guy at FAC this time. He's going to spot us an exit and pull some strings to keep us all safe.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: At the end of the day, ${PlayerName}'s back. His mere presence is enough to lift spirits. Let's play it like Raven does—leverage his fame for a few catchy slogans, make some ripples in the crowd.
steps.female_content: At the end of the day, ${PlayerName}'s back. Her mere presence is enough to lift spirits. Let's play it like Raven does—leverage her fame for a few catchy slogans, make some ripples in the crowd.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: And then there's you, Matilda Cavendish, our insider in Eastside. In just a year or two, the whole game could change—and you might be the political prodigy who reshapes destiny.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: 46 hours still on the clock. Detail work isn't really my thing. I'm gonna head out, see if I can find some new angles. I'm counting on you to look after the folks here.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Absolutely, I'll give it my all.
There lies Hecate in the hospital bed, with ${PlayerName} softly holding her hand at her side.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Really? The shackles still aren't fixed, and Hella's still out... Chief keeps pushing so hard...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Did I mess up somehow?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: The White Cube, painstakingly secured by many, was in my hands, and I couldn't get it to Chief in time.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I tripped and fell multiple times, clueless about where to head, wasting precious time...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Ran into some strangers but I couldn't push them away. I even left Nightmare behind, I couldn't fight at all as I went back...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I got lost, somehow made it back here to the base... because I didn't have enough info, and, well... I was clueless about what to do next, so my gut reaction was to seek help from somebody else...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I'm sorry, Chief. If I were stronger, more steadfast, I wouldn't have let us down. Then, you and Hella would have been completely healed by now.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: The fact that Hella is in this condition... it's my fault too...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...I'm so sorry, I am just too weak...

options: There's no need to say sorry for that, Hecate.

steps.content: If anyone should be apologizing, it's me. Breaking shackles only to let everyone down... I'm the one who should be saying sorry.
Your hand softly clasps hers, feeling the remnants of corruption on Hecate's skin. The weight of shackles is still present.
Forgive me, I wasn't powerful enough to keep you safe. But I refuse to give up, especially against those who've harmed you.
I promise to retrieve the shackles. But before I do, there's something I need from you.
Two hours on, fully prepared, Donald walks solo towards the High Tower.

steps.speaker: Alarm
steps.content: The Purge Order will commence in 43 hours. Attention all personnel, evacuate immediately, evacuate immediately.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: ...Okay, time to perk up and blaze a new trail.
He enters the Black Ring.
